title: I develop cozy game with AI
author: OpusGeo
selftext:
Hey everyone!

I'm working on my first solo game using Blender + Godot + generative AI tools (ComfyUI, GPT-4, etc).  
Along the way, I’ve been documenting every step — from prompt engineering to scene building and scripting.

I recently started a Skool group to share:
- 📦 Prompt packs for cozy game visuals, UI, levels  
- 🔧 My Godot/Blender pipeline (with lessons learned)  
- 🎥 Weekly breakdowns and devlog-style videos  
- 🎮 Real playable examples from my prototypes  

**Not a course, not a funnel — just a solo dev trying to build something, and help others do the same.**

If anyone else here is going through a similar journey or using AI to speed up their dev process, let’s connect and exchange ideas!

👉 https://www.skool.com/solo-game-dev-with-ai-2766/about?ref=66c26cb095c8450c9513df23ae349601  

🆓 **First 50 members join free**

Happy to answer any questions or show examples!

Great point — and thanks for raising it.

You're absolutely right: some of the clips are AI-rendered visuals, used for mood and direction — not actual gameplay. I always try to mention this in my posts, but I’ll make it more clear next time.

This project is very much in development — and I use a mix of AI and real builds to explore visual targets, then recreate them inside Godot/Blender step by step.

Appreciate the feedback 🙏

I was excited at the beginning but than I understood that gameplay videos are not real.   
The only real shots are when you show modeling process and some UI setup. 

But all the videos are fake.

I see nothing bad in using AI for anything but such concepts I would keep for myself as as reference of what I want and try to recreate the same feeling. 

But showing these videos as progress of your project is misleading.   
  
Or at least split your video into 2 parts. The one about the idea together with AI references and the other one about your current progress. Because after watching the video I have 0 clue of what is the actual progress.

No Lambos, no gurus — just one solo dev trying to build cool stuff and share the process openly.

You’re welcome to lurk, ask, or join if it ever feels worth it.
